If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I want an angular plate with two quadratic plates positioned in right angel to each other. The edge length of the plates is 140mm. They are 10mm thick. On one of the two plates I would like to have a quadratic cutout, 45x45mm, centred on the plate. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step implementation concept (functions only, no execution yet):

1. Build the first quadratic plate  
   • Use functions.block() to add one solid block.  
   • Dimensions: 140 mm (x) × 140 mm (y) × 10 mm (z → thickness).  
   • Base-point at the global origin (x=0, y=0, z=0).  
   • subtraction = False (it is the initial positive volume).

2. Build the second quadratic plate, oriented 90° to the first one (forming the “L”)  
   • Same function, same call, second entry in the parameter lists.  
   • Dimensions: 10 mm (x → thickness) × 140 mm (y) × 140 mm (z).  
   • Base-point also at (0, 0, 0).  
     – Because its 10 mm thickness lies along +X and the first plate’s 10 mm thickness lies along +Z, they overlap in a 10 × 10 × 10 mm cube and thus are rigidly connected along the common edge.  
   • subtraction = False.

3. Create the centred quadratic cut-out in the first plate  
   • Same block() call, third entry in the lists, but with subtraction=True.  
   • Cut-out size: 45 mm × 45 mm × 10 mm (full thickness of the bottom plate).  
   • Its centre must sit at the centre of the first plate (70 mm, 70 mm).  
     – Therefore its base-point is (70 – 22.5 = 47.5 mm, 70 – 22.5 = 47.5 mm, 0 mm).  
   • Setting subtraction=True removes this volume, leaving a through-hole.

4. Parameter arrays for one single functions.block() call  
   x_size       = [140,  10,  45]  
   y_size       = [140, 140,  45]  
   z_size       = [ 10, 140,  10]  
   x            = [  0,   0, 47.5]  
   y            = [  0,   0, 47.5]  
   z            = [  0,   0,   0]  
   subtraction  = [False, False, True]

5. After issuing this block() call, no other geometry functions are necessary; therefore a final functions.finished(allFunctionsCalled=True) should be sent afterwards (once you explicitly request execution).

When you say “prepare the function call,” I will supply the exact JSON payloads for block() and finished(), awaiting your final confirmation to execute.
